title: A general rule holds for every case
statement: A rule a lesson presents as true in general must hold for every case the lesson itself teaches.
example: One lesson's closing sentence was false for two of the five cases it taught.
detail: A reading lesson asked students to recite that every part keeps the plant alive, which is false for flowers and seeds, two of the five parts it taught, and contradicts the lesson's own rubric and closing text. The closing-questions spec requires the sentence to be true of every story or text, and the review notes that no mechanical check could tell this sentence was false; it took subject knowledge.

evidence.quote: **1. p24c `name-it` — the threshold sentence is false for two of the five parts the lesson teaches.**
